2010 Yuan silhouette: sail planes enter the tower, cruciform tail, single screw. Deck stays 0.0105 above the hull crown at the worst sample, including the bow. 2003 AMETHYSTE fit: fuller bow shoulder (radius still 0.66 at station 4.72 of 5) closing to a small tip cap, sail planes inside the tower, three masts. Deck clearance stays positive. This is the 73.6 m refit, not the 72.1 m original bow.

Early Akula: low sail (0.60 of hull height), bow planes, cruciform tail, and a stern pod. The pod overlaps the upper fin by 0.075 to 0.122 at the junction stations; the fore and aft overhang is outside that junction and is not scored as unsupported. Hull beam uses 13.8 m, not the 15.4 m overall breadth.

1980 first-series Sauro: sail planes inside the tower, cruciform tail, slim casing. Worst deck gap is 0.0096 at the bow station and still above the hull. The source page disagrees on the delivery date; the mesh is the 63.9 m by 6.83 m first-series shape only.

C-54G reads as a four-engine low-wing Skymaster: three-blade props, one fin, retracted tricycle, no tailwheel or weapons. Cockpit glass and cabin panes sit on the skin. Nose, cowlings and window count stay schematic versus the museum photos; the C-54D drawing was only a family plan.

C-119C reads as a Boxcar: two booms, two fins, connecting tailplane, short pod, closed clamshell seam, two four-blade props, retracted tricycle, no tailwheel, guns or JetPak. Authored anhedral is -1.5 degrees and looks nearly level. The C-119G outline was not copied as a C model.
